plans.note: Section 7 is captioned 'Limitations of Liability' — check whether the cap is mutual, tied to a meaningful amount (e.g., fees paid), and whether carve-outs (IP infringement, confidentiality, indemnity, willful misconduct) exist. Heading suggests a Contractor-favourable one-way structure.

Section 7 provides 'Indemnification of Contractor' — i.e., a customer-side indemnity running to RadialSpark. A Vendor-to-Customer IP/misconduct indemnity appears absent; also review the breadth of our indemnity in sec-7 and any IP warranty in sec-5 before concluding.
No covenant-style section in the outline; scan the scope/purpose language in sec-1 and any surviving covenants in sec-6 for restrictions on Clear Capital's business or competing products.
Check sec-1 (purpose/scope of engagement) and sec-3 (compensation) for any sole-source or exclusive-engagement language; none is signalled by the outline.
Pricing terms sit in sec-3; look for any most-favoured-customer obligation running against us. An MFN in our favour would be beneficial and not flagged.
No personnel/covenants section appears in the outline; check sec-6 for post-termination covenants and sec-1 for staffing language binding Clear Capital not to hire Contractor personnel.
Section 6 (Termination) is the locus: confirm we may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice without penalty or accelerated fees, and that Contractor cannot terminate at will mid-engagement.
Term/renewal mechanics are not visible (note the unlisted sec-2); check sec-6 and the preamble/Effective Date recitals for auto-renewal, notice window and renewal pricing before treating as absent.
No general/miscellaneous section is listed; boilerplate may sit in unnumbered closing text. Verify whether governing law and venue appear after sec-7 or in the preamble before recording as missing.
Assignment/change-of-control boilerplate is not in the outline; check the tail of the document and sec-6 for termination triggered by our change of control.

Section 4 governs ownership of materials and acceptance — confirm deliverables and Clear Capital data vest in us (work-for-hire plus assignment) and that no Clear Capital IP or data is assigned or licensed to Contractor.
Any licence-back or retained-tools licence should be in sec-4; check that it extends to our affiliates and contractors and is not revocable at Contractor's discretion.
No audit section listed; scan sec-3 (compensation/records) and sec-4 for any Contractor right to inspect our records or usage. If present, test frequency, notice and cost allocation.
Look for late-payment penalties, cancellation fees or stipulated damages in sec-3 and sec-6, and any liability language in sec-7; service credits running to us are welcome and not flagged.

Section 5 pairs Contractor warranties with a disclaimer — assess whether a services/Specifications warranty survives for a meaningful period with a real remedy, reading it with the acceptance mechanics in sec-4.
No insurance section appears; check sec-5 representations and any unlisted closing provisions. If Contractor handles our data or attends our premises, propose standard coverages.
Review sec-3 for minimum fees, guaranteed hours or take-or-pay commitments and sec-1 for committed volumes; nothing in the outline signals a minimum.

Section 6 may address effects of termination and sec-4 ownership/delivery of materials; confirm whether return of Clear Capital data and wind-down assistance are covered before treating the rule as missing.
